rule.note: The 1px boundary between modules, rows and sections.

ink-2.note: Labels, meta, muted values; also the info tone.

accent.note: Primary action, selection fill, live exception, module index tab. Never decoration.

accent-ink.note: Text and glyphs on the red fill.

accent-soft.note: Transient red wash only: the hop reveal's opening frame, a highlighted combobox row, a checked-row wash. Selection itself is a solid fill.

selection.note: Ambient selection wash token, defined but not used for selection; selected rows and chains take the solid utility red.

success.note: Healthy agent, chain, link and success notice. Always paired with a word.

danger.note: Failure text, danger borders, destructive actions, invalid fields. Crimson-pink family deliberately distinct from the utility red (dark #ff6b7a vs accent #ff3b2f; daylight #b3122f vs #e60012); never an ordinary action or a second accent.

brand-yellow.note: Preserved brand mark accent; brand material only, never a UI accent.

brand-mint.note: Preserved brand mark accent; brand material only, never a UI accent.

control.purpose: Buttons, navigation items, tabs and segmented controls.

motion.name: page-in

motion.name: hop-reveal

narrative.overview:
Lattix is one continuous ruled surface, not a page of cards. A near-black ground is divided by 1px rules into a mosaic of rectangular modules that tile edge to edge; the operator reads fleet totals, exceptions, server readings, throughput and runtime in one glance, then selects a server or chain and watches that selection take the one functional red. Nothing floats, nothing glows, and no decoration interrupts the scan. The world is Japanese contemporary high-density information web — small gothic type, dense rows, tabular numerals, and red used as a signal rather than a mood. Chinese headings speak in a self-hosted Noto Sans SC Black, Latin labels in Geist Variable, and changing metric figures in Barlow Condensed.

Dark is the default appearance and the primary rendering of the world; light is the same token system in daylight, not a second design language. Both appearances resolve identical slots (`--panel-*`), carry identical geometry (0–2px), identical rules (1px) and identical semantics, so a screen documented here is true in both. Both appearances add the same material concession: a 128px paper-grain tile on the page field — multiplied into the paper ground in daylight, screened faintly over the near-black ground in dark. In both appearances module heads close with a doubled hairline — a 1px rule plus a 50%-opacity inner rule — rather than a shaded band. The old `hig` / `cream` / `patchbay` themes and their cream paper, lime accents and equipment-metal metaphors are gone; there is a single visual language.

Hierarchy comes from three things only: rule weight (`--panel-rule` vs. `--panel-rule-strong`), tonal steps of the same hue (#0c0d0e ground → #111214 surface → #17181b raised → #0a0b0c inset), and the red index tab that names each module. Density is generous where it aids scanning (26–30px row heights, 8–10px cell padding) and never padded out for breathing room. Chinese copy stays Chinese; English uppercase appears only where it is a machine identifier — the module index tab, a column head, a panel state code.
keyCharacteristics: Flat near-black ground in dark, paper-white with a 128px paper-grain tile in light; no gradients, no glass, no colored side stripes.
Every boundary is a 1px hairline rule, doubled at module heads; modules are rectangles with 0–2px corners and a red index tab.
One functional red, used only for primary action, selection, and live exception.
Chinese page and dashboard headings in self-hosted Noto Sans SC Black at 900, Latin in Geist Variable, metric figures in Barlow Condensed, data rows in tabular mono.
Dense rectangular modules tiled edge to edge on a 6px gutter, not floating cards or hero metrics.
Zero shadows at rest; only overlays lift.
Motion is a single 180ms entrance and a one-shot hop reveal; reduced motion removes both.

rules.name: The One Functional Red Rule
rules.body: Red is a signal: primary action, current selection, live exception (carried by the danger step of the same family), and the module index tab. If red is not carrying one of those four meanings it is a defect — including decorative accents, section markers, gradients, and colored stripes.

rules.name: The Daylight Equivalence Rule
rules.body: Dark is the default appearance; light is the same token set in daylight, never a second palette. Any new surface must be built from `--panel-*` slots so it renders in both, and no component may be designed against one appearance only.

rules.name: The Two-State Rule
rules.body: Green and amber describe infrastructure state, red describes operator intent and exceptions. State colors are always carried by a word as well as a hue; a colored square alone is never the message.

rules.name: The Black Display Rule
rules.body: Chinese display headings are set in the self-hosted Noto Sans SC Black subset (page and dashboard titles at 900, the login statement at 900; the face declares a 700–900 range), stacked after Geist Variable and before the system CJK faces. It is the only Chinese display voice — no CDN face, no system serif, no faux-bold; Chinese body copy stays on the PingFang/Hiragino/YaHei/Noto CJK stack.

rules.name: The Tabular Numeral Rule
rules.body: Every figure that can change, or that sits in a column, is tabular — totals, throughput, latency, quota, cost, timestamps. Proportional figures are not used for data anywhere in the panel.

rules.name: The Chinese Copy Rule
rules.body: Interface copy stays Chinese. Uppercase Latin is reserved for machine identifiers and classification codes (module index tabs such as `FLEET` / `SERVERS` / `RUNTIME`, column heads, `ACTIVE` / `FAULTED` panel states, `NETWORK CONTROL PANEL` in the command bar) — never as an English restatement of a Chinese heading, never as a decorative eyebrow above a title. The access screen's headings now stand alone: the former `ACCESS` / `SIGN IN` eyebrow tabs are gone and do not return.

rules.name: The Dense Label Rule
rules.body: Labels and annotations may run as small as 9–10.5px because they are short and set in the gothic face; body copy never goes below 12px and table cells never below 11px, so density never costs legibility.

rules.name: The Edge-To-Edge Mosaic Rule
rules.body: Information tiles: modules share gutters and rules, align to one 12-column grid, and fill their rows. Floating cards with outer margins, centered hero metrics, and decorative empty space between modules are not part of this system.

rules.name: The Module Owns Its Scroll Rule
rules.body: A module's body scrolls inside its own ruled rectangle. A page-level scroll that hides a module's header — the tab and title that identify it — is a layout defect.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat until they are an overlay. No hover lift, no glow, no elevation animation; hover is a fill change (#17181b raised or the 4.5% hover wash) and active is a 1px downward shift on buttons.

rules.name: The No-Fake-Depth Rule
rules.body: No gradients, no glass, no backdrop blur, no inset highlight/shadow used to imitate material. If a boundary is needed, it is a 1px rule; if a step is needed, it is a tonal slot.

rules.name: The Paper Grain Rule
rules.body: Texture belongs only to the page field — a 128px paper-grain tile, multiplied in daylight and screened faintly in dark; the shell, modules and components stay flat. Module heads close with the doubled hairline (1px `--panel-rule` outer edge plus a 50%-opacity 1px `--panel-rule-strong` inner rule), never with a fill or a shadow. Grain is atmosphere, not a surface treatment: never inside a module, never as decoration on a component.

rules.name: The Two-Pixel Ceiling Rule
rules.body: Nothing in the working surface exceeds a 2px corner radius. Pills, capsules, 8px cards and circular buttons are outside the world; if a control asks for a rounder shape, it asks for the wrong control.

rules.name: The Rule-Not-Stripe Rule
rules.body: Separation is a hairline on an edge, not a colored side bar, a left accent stripe, or a gradient edge. The only filled edge in the system is the red index tab at a module's top-left.

rules.name: The Tab Opens The Module Rule
rules.body: A module without its red index tab is unrecognizable in this system: tab, Chinese title, and the doubled header hairline travel together. The tab names what the module is; it is not a decorative kicker and never sits above a page heading.

rules.name: The Selection Is Red Rule
rules.body: Current selection is expressed as a solid red fill across the entire row or chain, with inverted text and desaturated inner chips. Selection is never a border, a checkmark, a background tint plus stripe, or a hover-only state.

rules.name: The Chain Bench Rule
rules.body: One selected chain drives the hop strip; the selected server drives the runtime module. Each selection updates its module in place without navigating, and the hop strip reveals once per change rather than looping.

dos: Do build every screen as ruled modules on the 12-column mosaic with the 6px gutter and `--panel-*` tokens, so it renders identically in dark and light.
Do give each module its red index tab plus a Chinese title, and keep the header at 30px with the doubled hairline.
Do set Chinese page and dashboard headings in the self-hosted Noto Sans SC Black (900) and metric figures in Barlow Condensed; keep Chinese body copy on the system CJK stack.
Do keep the paper grain to the daylight body field (128px tile, multiply) and leave dark flat.
Do use tabular numerals for every figure and keep Chinese product copy in Chinese.
Do express selection as a full red fill with inverted text, and primary action as the single red button in its local group.
Do keep rows dense (26–30px) and align columns to the table's right edge for numbers.
Do preserve keyboard focus (`outline: 2px`, 1px offset), semantic status text, and `prefers-reduced-motion` opt-outs whenever a new surface is added.
Do let the selected server/chain update its module in place rather than pushing a new route.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent hue beyond the utility red and its danger step, a tinted surface, a gradient, or a colored side stripe.
Don't put decorative English eyebrows or kickers above Chinese headings; uppercase belongs to the module tab and machine codes, and the removed `ACCESS` / `SIGN IN` tabs stay removed.
Don't use the danger crimson for ordinary action or decoration; it is the fault step, not a second accent.
Don't color chart series with state green or amber; data series are grayscale plus one red.
Don't round above 2px, use pills for status, or turn modules into floating cards with outer shadows and margins.
Don't add shadows, glows, glass, or backdrop blur to in-page surfaces; overlay shadow only.
Don't lead a page with a hero metric or a marketing-style header block; the first viewport is the desk.
Don't encode state with color alone — a label or state word must carry it.
Don't depend on external font or texture CDNs; the panel must render fully self-hosted.
Don't reintroduce theme variants beyond appearance: one design language, shipped dark by default and light as its daylight version.
